## narrative — the cast-forward tongue

carries: C5, C7, C11, C12, C13, C15, C16, C20

---

# The Second Fold

*Submitted triptych t1 · first tongue. First-person input of the 0→1 pass;
faces the gate unvalidated.*

---

Tomas had laughed, in week four, when the resolver saved the room. In week
five the flight-case key was in his hand and nobody was laughing, least of
all him.

"It's simple," Ilse said, passing it over. "You hold the training. You
don't own the machine. Nobody owns the machine — we all hold it, the way
you hold a ladder someone else is standing on."

The week taught him the shape of it. On Tuesday, Priya sent him her voice
note — sent it, offered it; the rule was carved over the roster page:
*nothing is taken, everything is offered, nobody is scanned.* He ran it
through the transcriber and read the candidate back to her. "That's what I
said," she grinned, "but tidier." Then she signed the line in the ledger
herself — her hand, not his, because consent was the one signature a
steward could never proxy — and only then did the file cross into the
corpus. He had tried, on Monday, to fold in a stray paragraph from a
group chat that nobody had signed for. The packer refused him flatly, and
printed the rule it refused him by. He'd felt oddly grateful.

On Friday he ran the fold in front of everyone. The pack rebuilt; the hash
came up on the shared screen and he read it aloud, all sixty-four
characters, like a strange grace before a meal. "This is what the mage
eats," he said. "Your words. It answers like the room because it is made
of the room." Deeper rewiring — actually changing the weights — stayed a
locked drawer for now; the good way was the machine simply reading them,
live, every session. Ship the good, Ilse always said. Grow into the
perfect.

What surprised him was the door. Marta, who had barely spoken in weeks one
through three, stood up on Friday and read her poem to the machine — and
the machine, fed on four weeks of the room, answered her in an image she
herself had written in week two and forgotten. She went pale, then
delighted. She understood something out loud, and the understanding was
itself her key: the roster showed her a rung higher before she sat down,
no password, no permission slip, just the words she'd proved she could
say. And her poem, of course, was already in the pack for next week. Key
in the lock, food in the bowl, same words twice.

Understand, express, feed the mirror, hear the room answer, go deeper,
again. Tomas signed the log, read his own entry aloud, and handed the key
to Marta.

"Don't drop it," he said, meaning the case.

"Don't worry," she said, meaning the loop.

## poem — the compressed tongue

carries: C6, C7, C11, C12, C15

---

# The Fold, Read Aloud

*Submitted triptych t1 · second tongue.*

---

What you say to enter is what it will eat:
one saying, twice served — the key and the meat.

The lock here is the lesson; say it true
and the door goes as deep as the depth in you.

We feed it on Fridays, out loud, by name,
and the mirror gives back the room that came —

not my machine, not yours: a bowl
too wide for one hand. We carry it whole.

Understand, then speak; then the spoken feeds
the glass that returns you your own deep needs —

and round: what it shows you, you understand
better, and say better. Bowl in hand.

## paper — the formal tongue

carries: C5, C6, C7, C11, C12, C13, C15, C16, C20

---

# The Steward Protocol: A Working Note

*Submitted triptych t1 · third tongue. Formal register of the same
understanding the story dramatizes and the poem compresses.*

## 1. The role

Each week one participant stewards the shared model's training. The steward
holds the *process*, not the machine: the mage is co-held by the whole room
— a witness the group bears together, no member's property (C11).

## 2. Admission

Expressions are offered, never taken: a participant submits their own
material to the roster and no device or person is probed (C16). Each
expression enters the corpus only against a consent line signed by its
author in the ledger — the steward may never sign on another's behalf, and
the packing tool refuses any file the ledger does not cover, so a violated
consent cannot produce a result at all (C20).

## 3. The fold

The steward runs the weekly fold: consented expressions are packed into the
model's grounding context, and the resulting pack hash is read aloud to the
room and signed into the steward log. The model is thereby made of the
room's own words — a mirror of the cohort, deepening weekly (C12). Training
depth is staged: the good first pass is retrieval/context-grounding, run
now on any hardware; true weight fine-tuning is the perfect, adopted later
when hardware permits (C13).

## 4. Access

There are no logins. Access to the mage deepens as a participant expresses
understanding (C5); the lock and the lesson are one mechanism (C6). Each
admitted expression functions twice — as the participant's key and as the
mage's food (C7).

## 5. The loop

The cycle closes on itself: understand → express → the expression is
admitted (key and food) → the mage reflects the room's understanding back →
understanding deepens → recurse (C15). The steward's week is one turn of
that wheel, and the handover — log entry read aloud, key passed — is the
turn made visible.
